Ui.Script:
CASTING_BAR_ALPHA_STEP = 0.05 CASTING_BAR_FLASH_STEP = 0.2 CASTING_BAR_HOLD_TIME = 1
-- The ref applies the two steps PER OnUpdate TICK (no arg1 scaling) — the flash/fade -- tail is frame-rate dependent by the reference's own design: ~25 ticks from hold-expiry -- to hidden, i.e. 0.83 s at the reference bottle's configured cap (WoW/WTF/Config.wtf -- `SET maxfps "30"`), 0.42 s at an era-typical 60 fps, a blink at 120. We render fast, -- so the step lines below are normalized to the reference tick rate — the bar's -- hold+fade then matches the reference window at any render rate (decision 0454). CASTING_BAR_REF_TICK = 30
-- The 1.12 GlobalStrings values (no GlobalStrings.lua is loaded yet). FAILED = FAILED or "Failed" INTERRUPTED = INTERRUPTED or "Interrupted"
-- THE BAR'S WHOLE VOCABULARY, one entry per wire event, each taking the frame. OnLoad -- registers this table's keys and OnEvent looks the incoming event up in it, so the set -- the bar LISTENS for and the set it can ANSWER are the same set by construction — there -- is no second list to fall out of step with. (The reference spells both halves out: eight -- RegisterEvent calls, then a sixty-line if-chain testing the same eight strings back.) local castingBarEvent = {}
-- Seat the fill at `value` and ride the spark on its leading edge. The bar is 195px wide, -- so a fraction of `span` scales straight to a pixel offset from the frame's LEFT. A cast -- and a channel differ only in which value and which span they hand in. local function castingBarTrack(bar, value, span) bar:SetValue(value) CastingBarFlash:Hide() local sparkPosition = ((value - bar.startTime) / span) * 195 -- Pushback slides startTime PAST the wall clock, so a cast really can sit before its -- own window's start for a frame or two. (A channel cannot — its value counts down -- from the far end and stops at startTime — so here the clamp is dead weight rather -- than a change of behaviour.) if sparkPosition < 0 then sparkPosition = 0 end CastingBarSpark:SetPoint("CENTER", CastingBarFrame, "LEFT", sparkPosition, 2) end
-- A cast opens: orange, a full window anchored on the clock, the spark at the left edge. castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_START = function(bar) bar:SetStatusBarColor(1.0, 0.7, 0.0) CastingBarSpark:Show() bar.startTime = GetTime() bar.maxValue = bar.startTime + (arg2 / 1000) bar:SetMinMaxValues(bar.startTime, bar.maxValue) bar:SetValue(bar.startTime) CastingBarText:SetText(arg1) bar:SetAlpha(1.0) bar.holdTime = 0 bar.casting = 1 bar.fadeOut = nil bar:Show() end
-- A channel opens. Its args are START's the other way round — milliseconds first, then the -- name — and its fill DRAINS, so the bar is seated at the far end and walks back. castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_START = function(bar) bar:SetStatusBarColor(1.0, 0.7, 0.0) CastingBarSpark:Show() bar.maxValue = 1 bar.startTime = GetTime() bar.endTime = bar.startTime + (arg1 / 1000) bar.duration = arg1 / 1000 bar:SetMinMaxValues(bar.startTime, bar.endTime) bar:SetValue(bar.endTime) CastingBarText:SetText(arg2) bar:SetAlpha(1.0) bar.holdTime = 0 bar.casting = nil bar.channeling = 1 bar.fadeOut = nil bar:Show() end
-- The server's mid-channel correction: the window keeps its LENGTH and is re-anchored to -- end arg1 ms from now, so a pushback eats into what is left rather than extending it. castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_UPDATE = function(bar) if not bar:IsShown() then return end local span = bar.endTime - bar.startTime bar.endTime = GetTime() + (arg1 / 1000) bar.startTime = bar.endTime - span bar:SetMinMaxValues(bar.startTime, bar.endTime) end
-- Pushback on taking a hit (SMSG_SPELL_DELAYED, decision 0256): BOTH ends of the window -- slide out by arg1 ms, so the cast has that much longer to run and the spark jumps back. -- A hit never cancels the bar. castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_DELAYED = function(bar) if not bar:IsShown() then return end local pushback = arg1 / 1000 bar.startTime = bar.startTime + pushback bar.maxValue = bar.maxValue + pushback bar:SetMinMaxValues(bar.startTime, bar.maxValue) end
-- The cast landed, or a channel ran its course: green, full, and the completion bloom -- armed at alpha 0 for OnUpdate to ramp. `flag` names the one field the event clears, -- which is the only thing that separates the two of them. local function castingBarFinished(bar, flag) if not bar:IsShown() then return end bar:SetValue(bar.maxValue) bar:SetStatusBarColor(0.0, 1.0, 0.0) CastingBarSpark:Hide() CastingBarFlash:SetAlpha(0.0) CastingBarFlash:Show() bar[flag] = nil bar.flash = 1 bar.fadeOut = 1 end castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_STOP = function(bar) castingBarFinished(bar, "casting") end castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_CHANNEL_STOP = function(bar) castingBarFinished(bar, "channeling") end
-- The cast did NOT land: red, the reason where the spell's name was, and held opaque for -- CASTING_BAR_HOLD_TIME before the fade starts — no completion bloom. A channel is never -- ended this way (the server closes one with CHANNEL_STOP), so a live channel ignores both. local function castingBarAborted(bar, reason) if not bar:IsShown() or bar.channeling then return end bar:SetValue(bar.maxValue) bar:SetStatusBarColor(1.0, 0.0, 0.0) CastingBarSpark:Hide() CastingBarText:SetText(reason) bar.casting = nil bar.fadeOut = 1 bar.holdTime = GetTime() + CASTING_BAR_HOLD_TIME end castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_FAILED = function(bar) castingBarAborted(bar, FAILED) end castingBarEvent.SPELLCAST_INTERRUPTED = function(bar) castingBarAborted(bar, INTERRUPTED) end
function CastingBarFrame_OnLoad() local bar = this for spellcast in pairs(castingBarEvent) do bar:RegisterEvent(spellcast) end bar.casting = nil bar.holdTime = 0 -- The alias global the reference publishes at the end of its own OnLoad -- (`CastingBarFrame.lua:16`). `CastingBarFrame` IS the StatusBar in 1.12 — there is no -- separate child frame — so the name an addon reaches for has to resolve to the frame -- itself. -- -- 11 corpus addons index `CastingBarFrameStatusBar`, and it was the largest single -- name in the whole session-start `attempt to index global` row. It went missing here -- once and nothing warned: a line dropped from INSIDE a function is invisible to every -- instrument we have. `framexml-transcription-diff.py` compares elements and handlers, -- not function bodies, and would not even pair these two files (ours is CastingBar.xml, -- the reference's is CastingBarFrame.xml). CastingBarFrameStatusBar = bar bar:Hide() end
function CastingBarFrame_OnEvent() local handle = castingBarEvent[event] if handle then handle(this) end end
function CastingBarFrame_OnUpdate() local bar = this if bar.casting then -- The fill IS the wall clock, pinned at the window's end once the cast is spent. local now = GetTime() if now > bar.maxValue then now = bar.maxValue end castingBarTrack(bar, now, bar.maxValue - bar.startTime) elseif bar.channeling then local now = GetTime() if now >= bar.endTime then bar.channeling = nil bar.fadeOut = 1 return end -- A channel drains: the value is the window's start plus what is LEFT of it, so -- the fill empties from full instead of filling from empty. castingBarTrack(bar, bar.startTime + (bar.endTime - now), bar.endTime - bar.startTime) elseif GetTime() < bar.holdTime then return elseif bar.flash then local alpha = CastingBarFlash:GetAlpha() + CASTING_BAR_FLASH_STEP * (arg1 * CASTING_BAR_REF_TICK) if alpha < 1 then CastingBarFlash:SetAlpha(alpha) else CastingBarFlash:SetAlpha(1.0) bar.flash = nil end elseif bar.fadeOut then local alpha = bar:GetAlpha() - CASTING_BAR_ALPHA_STEP * (arg1 * CASTING_BAR_REF_TICK) if alpha > 0 then bar:SetAlpha(alpha) else bar.fadeOut = nil bar:Hide() end end end
